text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance minister Mudavadi will seek parliament's approval for an estimated 2.3 billion shillings to finance general elections scheduled for later in year.

- International Cricket Council grants Kenya One Day International Status, which means one-day matches involving Kenya will be considered "first class" and gives Kenya automatic entry into next cricket World Cup in year 2003.
- Eighteen foreign missions in Nairobi urge government and pro-constitutional reform lobby groups to engage in dialogue to avert violence.
- Opposition leaders Kenneth Matiba and Raila Odinga say reform rallies planned for Saturday have been cancelled.
- Pope extremely worried by brutal armed attack that seriously wounded three nuns at Pope's envoy's residence in Nairobi.
- Moslem leaders put pressure on government to give back controversial preacher and leading government critic Sheikh Khalid Balala his Kenyan citizenship.
- Bishop Bernard Njoroge of Church of the Province of Kenya (Anglican) quits service and condemns Kenya's Anglican church leadership for what he calls lack of morals and vision.
- Five foreign missions in Kenya, among them U.S., say they back proposed Peaceful Assemblies Bill that seeks to replace contentious Public Order Act.
- Provincial administration and Nairobi City Council say they will not give in to any pressures whatsoever to let hawkers back into Nairobi's main commercial district.
